name: Austerity of body, speech and mind

names.name: Austerity of body, speech and mind

method_summary: Bodily: worship of gods, the twice-born, teachers and the wise; purity, straightforwardness, celibacy, non-harming (17.14). Verbal: speech that does not agitate, true, pleasant and beneficial, and the practice of recitation (17.15). Mental: clarity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-restraint, purity of disposition (17.16). It is sāttvic when practised with supreme faith by the disciplined who do not desire its fruit (17.17).

warnings.text: Austerity done for respect, honour and reverence, or with hypocrisy, is rājasic, unstable and impermanent.
Austerity done from a deluded notion, with torment of oneself or to ruin another, is tāmasic.
Terrible austerity not enjoined by scripture, done with hypocrisy and egoism, tormenting the body's elements and the Lord within, marks those of demonic resolve.

name: Sāttvic food
method_summary: The text classifies foods by the type of person to whom they are dear: foods increasing life, sattva, strength, health, happiness and delight, savoury, smooth, substantial and agreeable, are dear to the sāttvic (17.8); pungent, sour, salty, very hot, sharp, dry and burning foods, which bring pain, grief and disease, to the rājasic (17.9); stale, tasteless, putrid, overnight, leftover and impure food to the tāmasic (17.10). It states effects but gives no explicit rule of diet.

warnings.text: Rājasic foods bring pain, grief and disease.

name: Giving (dāna)
method_summary: Give because it ought to be given, to one who makes no return, at the right place and time, to a worthy recipient (sāttvic, 17.20); giving is not to be abandoned but done without attachment and fruit (18.5–6).

warnings.text: Giving for a return, for fruit or grudgingly is rājasic.
Giving at the wrong place and time, to the unworthy, without respect and with contempt is tāmasic.

name: Sacrifice and eating its remains (yajña, yajña-śiṣṭa)

names.name: Sacrifice and eating its remains (yajña, yajña-śiṣṭa)

method_summary: Summary as chs. 17–18 state it (no procedure is given): sacrifice offered according to injunction by those not desiring its fruit, the mind set on 'it simply ought to be offered', is sāttvic (17.11); the rites of the expounders of Brahman begin with 'oṃ' (17.24); sacrifice, giving and austerity purify the wise, are not to be abandoned, and are to be done giving up attachment and fruit (18.5–6).

warnings.text: Sacrifice for fruit or display is rājasic.
Sacrifice without injunction, distributed food, mantras, fee or faith is tāmasic.
Sacrifices in name only, with hypocrisy and not by injunction, are the demonic's.

name: Performing rites with 'oṃ tat sat'
method_summary: Summary as the text states it: the acts of sacrifice, giving and austerity of the expounders of Brahman begin with the utterance of 'oṃ' (17.24); with 'tat', those seeking release perform sacrifice, austerity and giving without aiming at fruit (17.25); 'sat' is applied to what is real and good, to praiseworthy acts, to steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and giving, and to action for that purpose (17.26–27). The three words are the threefold designation of Brahman (17.23).

warnings.text: Whatever is offered, given, practised or done without faith is 'asat', of no account here or hereafter.

notes: This edition's 17.23 omits 'oṃ' (see the teaching's notes).

name: Relinquishing the fruit of all actions

names.name: Relinquishing the fruit of all actions

method_summary: Do sacrifice, giving, austerity and obligatory action because they ought to be done, giving up attachment and fruit (18.6, 18.9); since the embodied cannot give up action entirely, relinquishing the fruit of action makes one a relinquisher (18.2, 18.11).
signs_of_progress: The relinquisher, pervaded by sattva, intelligent, doubts cut, neither hates disagreeable action nor clings to agreeable action (18.10).

warnings.text: Abandoning obligatory action out of delusion is tāmasic relinquishment.
Abandoning action because it is painful, from fear of bodily hardship, is rājasic and gains no fruit of relinquishment.

name: Relinquishment before action (sāttvika-tyāga)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 18.9: doing obligatory action simply because it is to be done, giving up attachment and fruit — the sāttvic relinquishment.

name: Performing one's own duty (svakarma)
method_summary: Be devoted to one's own work (18.45) and worship with it him from whom beings arise and by whom all is pervaded (18.46); keep one's own dharma though deficient rather than another's, and do not abandon the work born with one even if faulty (18.47–48).

name: The Gītā's meditation (dhyāna-yoga, BhG 6.10–32)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 18.51–53: yoked with a purified understanding, restraining oneself with steadiness, relinquishing sound and the other objects, casting off passion and aversion, resorting to solitude, eating lightly, controlling speech, body and mind, ever intent on the yoga of meditation, taking refuge in dispassion, letting go of ahaṅkāra, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessions, without 'mine' and at peace.
prerequisites: The perfection (siddhi) of 18.49–50, from which the course to Brahman is described.
signs_of_progress: Fitness for becoming Brahman (18.53); the one become Brahman is serene, neither grieves nor craves, is the same to all beings and attains supreme devotion (18.54).

name: Dispassion (vairāgya)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 18.52: taking refuge in dispassion, within the discipline of 18.51–53.

name: Non-possessiveness (aparigraha)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 18.53: letting go of possessions (parigraha), without 'mine', within the discipline of 18.51–53.

name: Resigning all actions to the Lord (mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasya)

names.name: Resigning all actions to the Lord (mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasya)

method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 18.57: renouncing in thought all actions in the Lord, intent on him, resorting to the yoga of understanding, with thought constantly on him; so one crosses all difficulties by his grace (18.58).

name: Buddhiyoga, the yoga of understanding (BhG 2.39–53)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 18.57: resorting to the yoga of understanding while renouncing all actions in the Lord in thought and keeping thought on him.

name: Taking refuge in the Lord alone (śaraṇāgati)

names.name: Taking refuge in the Lord alone (śaraṇāgati)

method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 18.56, 18.62, 18.66: taking refuge in the Lord even while always performing all actions; going to him alone for refuge with one's whole being; abandoning all dharmas and going to him alone for refuge, who promises release from all sins.
signs_of_progress: By grace, the eternal imperishable state (18.56), supreme peace and the eternal abode (18.62), release from all sins (18.66).

name: Bowing to the Lord (namaskāra)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 18.65: 'bow to me', with mind on the Lord, devotion to him and sacrifice to him (repeating 9.34).

name: Study and hearing of the Gītā

names.name: Study and hearing of the Gītā

method_summary: Declaring the supreme secret among the Lord's devotees with supreme devotion (18.68), the dearest service (18.69); studying the dialogue, which is worship by the sacrifice of knowledge (18.70); or merely hearing it with faith and without cavil, which brings the worlds of the meritorious (18.71).
prerequisites: The hearer is not to be one without austerity, without devotion, unwilling to listen, or cavilling at the Lord (18.67).

warnings.text: The teaching must never be told to one without austerity or devotion, one unwilling to listen, or one who cavils at the Lord.

name: Non-harming (ahiṃsā)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 16.2, 17.14: a mark of the divine endowment and part of bodily austerity.

name: Truthfulness (satya)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 16.2, 17.15: a mark of the divine endowment; true, pleasant, beneficial and non-agitating speech is the austerity of speech.

name: Purity (śauca)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 16.3, 17.14, 18.42: a mark of the divine endowment, part of bodily austerity and of the brāhmaṇa's work.

name: Self-study (svādhyāya)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 16.1, 17.15: one's own recitation of scripture is a mark of the divine endowment, and its practice (svādhyāya-abhyasana) part of the austerity of speech.
